text:
They pull shots for real, here! Pretty impressive. I daresay the only place in New Orleans that does so. At least as far as I've noticed.

I kind of dig it all: cozy coffee shop ambiance with tons of outlets and free wifi; outside seating is pretty goddamned idyllic (you are surrounded by the fabulous Marigny, after all). I haven't yet tried any of the food here, but my friends all seemed pretty happy with what they ordered for brunch, so I'll go with that. 

People who need peace and quiet take note: inside is often as quiet as a graveyard. 

Look for my update once I eat something from the kitchen.

Oh and helllllo vegan baked goods!

Okay, so I love District Donuts. They're definitely purveyors of the Nouveau Orleanian vibe that's been a steady undercurrent in the restaurant scene for the last few years. But despite (or maybe in spite) of the on-trend, almost too-hip exposed brick/metal pipe/Edison bulb interior aesthetic they deliver on the inventive donut and coffee (and slider, after 11am) front. 

"But wait!" you might be saying. "This is supposed to be a review for District Hand Pie + Coffee!" And if you were saying that, you would be right. Good for you. Consider my last paragraph a necessary preface and read on with the knowledge you've gained from it:

District Hand Pie + Coffee is the newest extension of the DDSB crew. They've kept the coffee menu from the original location but besides that, everything else about their menu is new and different and dare I say, fantastic. They only deal in hand pies - warm, flaky little pockets of goodness, the contents of which change daily. For their opening day they had available kung pao chicken, shepherd's pie, cherry basil, and blueberry creole cream cheese pies, to give you an idea. In addition to the standard coffee menu there's also a "craft coffee" menu which includes enough fancy coffee drinks to get John L. H.'s knickers in a twist for days on end. 

For my first visit I had one of the shepherd's pie and cherry basil hand pies, with an Under 'Spro to wash it all down. The hand pies were delicious. The cherry basil was not too sweet and had the right amount of fresh basil flavor to it and the shepherd's pie was a good balance of savory with a little bit of sweetness coming from the roasted carrots on top. The Under 'Spro was a layered drink served shooter style that consisted of perfectly brewed espresso, cream, and root beer syrup. Prices are reasonable--expect to pay between 5-6$ for a hand pie and the fancy coffee drinks are all between 3.50-5$. One pie is good for a light meal or snack and two will do you for a full meal, I'd say.

Even if none of this sounds appealing to you (which would be a shame, really, and possibly a sign of a bigger problem) you should still stop by the shop at least once just to LOOK at it. It's in the same tiny location that used to house Velvet Espresso but they've completely transformed it into something unique and gorgeous. Stunning parquet floors and a gigantic butcher block counter, as well as tap handles made from old tools and a vaulted ceiling with a stained-glass "skylight". The walls are decorated with hand painted pieces by L.A.-based street artist Wrdsmth so everywhere you look there's something to neat to read. There are a few seats outside the building in front and a small deck at the back with some chairs on it as well so you don't have to worry about quickly scarfing your delicious food over the espresso bar while the nice guys and gals who work there stare at you with puzzled expressions on their faces. 


In short: why are you still reading this? You should be there already.

We've been eating here coming up to 7 years now.  If anything, the food has gotten better.  I can't say I have a real favorite.  I'll select pasta dishes from all over the menu.  I like the idea that they have both small and large plates for most of the pasta dishes, to suit my hunger.  If pressed for a favorite, then it is probably the veal parmesan.  My wife's favorite entrée is the eggplant parmesan.  Over the first part of last year, I don't know how many times she sent me here to pick up an order of the eggplant for her.  I'm glad that they are now open again for inside dining.

Pro's: Everything
Con's: Not one thing
Go back?: Already becoming a regular

More...
This review is specifically for the new Rancharrah location. I have eaten there twice this week! The first time, I had the Croque Madame....eu la la! So fresh and delicious. The fries are great...can't wait to try the truffle fries sometime soon. I loved it so much, I brought my husband out on Saturday. He had the fish and eggs and LOVED it. I had the cheddar grits with a fried egg and all the other yummies they added to that bowl. Amazing! How do they get a fried egg to look like it is sunny-side up, but is not, but is still cooked right to the edge of the yolk? Unbelievable! The creativity of unique flavors found here is refreshing and a real treat. Sunday morning, I woke up wanting more Perenn but know I can't eat cheddar grits every day...but I was really craving their dark roast COFFEE. Wow. I can go back for coffee...and maybe a little chocolate bouchon.

It was busy when we were there on Saturday. There was a table but it had no chairs. The server went and fetched chairs from outside without our even asking.

There is also a market area where we bought fig and rosemary garlic bread. That was amazing with dinner last night? Who thinks of these combos? So delicious! We also bought the pistachio and pork pate....YUM! Husband wanted the sardines...I'm sure he will like them - not my thing.

There was a mistake on my order which was quickly rectified and to make amends, they gave me a chocolate chip cookie. You guys can screw up my order ANY TIME! Hahahaha.

Perenn is NOT TO BE MISSED IN RENO.

I have eaten here a few times and every time everything was spot on! The bubbly juice wasn't so bubbly but that's probably the only thing I could complain about! The smoked salmon Benedict was TO DIE FOR. As well as the farmhouse Benedict. This place carries first watch vibes. But is in their own line completely. My husband had oatmeal pancakes and they were also amazing. Highly recommend I will most definitely be back!

Who would put pepperoni, tomatoes, and caramelized onions on a burger and call it "Antique Row"? The answer: a genius.  

This is the typical pizza place with an extensive menu.  Not only are there pizzas, specialty pizzas, and pastas, there are also burgers, sandwiches, and salads.  This much selection is common in many pizza shops in Philly/South Jersey.  

What isn't typical about this pizza shop is the quality of food. Try a couple of different slices, when you go, and you'll be very happy.  Really, try anything, when you go, and you'll be happy.   They make the food when you order, so it's always hot when it reaches your mouth.  And that, I think, is the only way to eat a pizza.

The only thing that's a little strange is this: there's a little square between the steaks and the chicken sandwiches on the menu.  It's hard to notice and comprehend, so I'll tell you what it says. "Our chicken cheesesteak is fresh chicken breast marinated in olive oil & fresh squeezed lemon".  Even if you notice it on the menu, you assume that it can't apply to the buffalo chicken cheesesteak you're ordering... But it does apply to you. So if you order a chicken cheesesteak, you're actually just ordering a chicken sandwich with large pieces of meat.  It's clearly stated on the menu, but I've seen people order it and get disappointed (until they took that first bite, that is).   

Also, check out the walls.  After you get distracted by the cute, cartoonish foods on the walls, you'll notice that they have pictures of local musicians and other locals hanging, too.  I support a pizza shop that supports local musicians.

Came in for the Common Thread Noodle Tour and tried out the special dish they created for it. WOW, I have never had something with so many different unique flavors. It was like a Japanese style spaghetti with all the right hints of flavors. The Tsuyunashi Tantamen is definitely so
Etching is love to see on the normal menu. It was really homey and comforting and the perfect meal to end a long day. 

I was also impressed with the huge selection of different spirits, beer, and sale they had. And we got a few items from the yakitori grill and they all came with little thoughtful accompaniments that added to the flavors and textures of the different grilled meats.

Delicious thali-style Indian lunch today at this new undiscovered place in Morrisville.

We were the only lunch customers and were treated like special guests. Two of us chose the chicken and one the veggie special. Each was served with naan bread, basmati rice, a small soup, dal, and a yogurt chutney and a small dessert. The veggie had saag paneer & the others chicken tikka masala. We loved everything. The chicken was tender and delicious. We were stuffed but shared a kulfi ice cream that was pink and  tasted delicious with rosewater notes and nuts.

I worry if this place will make it unless people give it a try. I figure if an Afghani place in Morrisville is doing well, maybe folks with try this Indian fusion that has  many dishes from other countries even Pad Thai.

We'll be back...you should try it!

A trip to Saraga is not just shopping, it's an adventure.   If 
Walmart mated with a corner Asian grocery, Saraga would be the offspring.  It is a huge grocery with rows and rows of ethnic food from all over the world, but with a concentration from Asian countries.  The building it is in used to be a Super K-MART, so that should give you an idea of how big it is.  It has a green grocery and a meat, dairy, and fish counter to boot.   Great place to get some esoteric food stuffs.   The smell might be off putting to some, because it has that Marketplace smell, with overtones of fish, ripe produce and exotic spices, but to me that just adds to the atmosphere.  One day I decided to make my own sushi and bought the salmon (sushi grade), the rice (huge rice selection), the seaweed wraps, the rice vinegar, and the Daikon pickle right there.   You can even buy sushi knifes there.  The prices are reasonable and fair and I've found you can actually buy some ethnic foods (such as Mexican) cheaper there than at the regular grocery.   If you like exotic food and cultures, you will be fascinated by the many different products (who knew the Japanese are so picky about salt).  I recommend this as a great place to visit if you are planning an ethnic meal.

place is OVERRATED! service was absolutely terrible, the staff was rude as h*ll. (excuse my language) the food didn't taste good at all- honestly frozen lasagna tastes better. the lasagna didn't even have ricotta cheese... WHAT LASAGNA DOESN'T HAVE RICOTTA CHEESE. it was just noodles & sauce basically, with no flavor. same goes for the spaghetti. we definitely will not be back.

MMMM! MMMM! MMMM! 

Nick's Italian Deli is an actual NY place, it seems family run (which is cool) and their food is delicious!!!! DELICIOUS!!!!!!

We ordered the only size they have, X-LG, pizza with pepperoni, onions & garlic and it was FANTASTIC! The fresh cheese, the sauce, the dough and the ingredients were all of the highest quality! 

We'd never been to Nick's before and thanks to Yelp, we found this gem! It's off a little side street (Alpha), just off 31, near the Franklin Target (Mack Hatcher & 31, if you're looking for big streets). The inside is full of Italian decor and is super clean. What's really nice is, if you order your pizza for pick up (not dining inside)... they have a very convenient drive thru window (just make sure you give them 20 minutes or so to make your pie)! 

If you don't want a whole one... they have calzone's, pizza by the slice and an impressive menu of antipasto and salads. In addition, I noticed they also offer lunch specials and deals on their facebook page (http://www.facebook.com/pages/Franklin-TN/Nicks-Italian-Deli-and-Pizzeria/116924078346855?v=wall). 

We hadn't planned to get anything but a pizza... but their homemade desserts we're just too good to pass up. We procured their tiramisu (some of the best I've had) and a spumoni cheesecake (if you like spumoni & cheesecake... it's a MUST HAVE!). 

If you're going to dine in... be sure to visit on Tuesday's... they have $2 long necks and it's always BYOW (bring your own wine)! 

As a side note... they are closed on Sunday & Monday! 

For the BEST pizza and Italian food in general, visit Nick's... you'll be totally hooked, we are!

First visit after the recommendation from a co-worker and we were so pleased...
The lentil soup was smooth, well-spiced with something intriguing and served piping hot. My chicken shwarma plate was perfect with well-seasoned chicken that had some lovely crispness. The rice pilaf was so well-flavored I could have made a meal of it. The salad had crisp deep green lettuce, tasty tomatoes, feta and ripe olives. It was a large platter for the $10 price, and really a delight for the palate.
This is a very small place,very casual and food is served quickly. I noticed they offer family meals for takeaway at reasonable prices.
Looks like we have found another Tucson gem!

P.s. In response to a low star review complaining about the ground meat kebabs ... The menu clearly describes the kebabs as "ground sirloin" ... I wonder How can you be surprised?

If instantly taking on the aromas of an ashtray makes you feel very upset, you'll probably want to pass on Paddy's. I do not smoke anymore, but I know what I'm getting into if we stop in for a drink, which we are occasionally want to do if we're in the neighborhood. Sweet freedom, smokers! Inside smoking, you'll find it here...
Anyway, we're always met with friendliness in this tiny dive. Instantly comfortable. I like it.

There's no food to be had here, but you will find a pretty ok good selection of beers, and jukebox tunes. Admittedly, we're not typically ones to frequent Paddy's during the busy business of Ye Olde City's weekend hullabaloo... We're more likely to be in the area on slow Sunday nights, or so. One such visit, during my still-smoking-menthols age, was marked by drinking and smoking while all on the rail quietly watched The Discovery Channel on TV. Sharks. I always remember that night as if it were a scene from a strange, strange movie.

Absolutely disappointing. After going out of my way to drive down to this Viva Burrito I'm met with nothing more than an excessively annoying experience and the urge to write my first yelp review. First off, as I said before the drive to this location is enough to be considered a 'labour of love.' I really like Viva and have never had a negative experience. However this time was different... It started with the famous Viva drive through at about 12:45am: there I was, seemingly alone. I asked 'hello?' once, twice... Nothing. Then I drove around to check to see if there were even any employees about. Yep, there they were. So I thought maybe another round directly to the drive through window would work. I honked my horn, still nothing. Again... Silence. By this time somebody had walked into the shop to order. Bless him. I sat outside and *eagerly* watched as he waited, and waited, and waited without anybody helping him. Needless to say, I left hungry. Is a late night carne asada burrito that much to ask for? I didn't think so, however I've been proven wrong tonight. Thanks for nothing (except for an empty stomach and a fuller wallet) Viva.

Love this place!!! Can't believe I am a Santa Barbara local born and raised and this is my first time trying it!!! Boy have I been missing out!!
First of the chocolate croissant is very yummy!!! 
 Great outdoor seating so if you bring your dog you can still enjoy a good breakfast on the patio. 
We had the french toast and wow was it good!!
The bread they use makes it very yummy and the fruit to go with it was delicious!! Nice to find a place that doesn't charge $3 plus dollars to add fruit to french toast to make it a tad bit healthier.
I feel like lately I have been on a mission to find the best french toast in Santa Barbara and so far this one has beat out 5 other restaurants!
Amazing spot!!! I will definitely be back!!

I am pumped to have Los Camaradas so close to where I live! I've had dinner there three times so far and I'm loving what Joe and Theresa have brought to the neighborhood.

I'm a huge fan of margaritas and the ones served at Los Camaradas are delicious and on point. They use quality ingredients, nothing fake, and you can taste the difference. They go down easy. They also have a nice beer selection including a pilsner on draft named after the restaurant which pairs perfectly with the food. 

Speaking of the food, I love that they have a nice mix of guilty pleasure foods as well as some items that lean towards the healthier side. Their nachos are on point, and I personally love the oozy cheese that they use in addition to all of the other great toppings. The tortilla soup is definitely a favorite, and I really enjoyed the Los Camaradas salad topped with shrimp on my most recent visit. I've also had the chuleta de puerco: thick slices of perfectly seasoned lean pork served with black beans and plantain rice. 

I'm looking forward to trying brunch and am crossing my fingers for happy hour, because the only thing better than a margarita is several margaritas at a discount.

I'm actually amazed I have not written a review here yet.
Solid 5 stars!!!!

OMG. Delicious Aroma slams your face the minute you walk into the door, yes. Even with a mask on the aroma is soooo delicious. 

Will start with the establishment before I get into the details of their items. 

Location is a bit hidden, my husband was actually the one who found this place on Yelp. Not really my stomping ground, so unless you planned on going in specifically or happened to stumble across the other small business in the area it really is hidden.  Parking is limited, but every time I have gone in was still able to find parking up front. 

Establishment is very clean, staff is always friendly and seems to be a family owned/run. 
Which is a win #Support local business 

My husband is tall enough to catch a glimpse of someone making the Sausages by hand and just adds on to the whole excitement of wanting to eat it asap!

Okay, let's get down with the food. 
#1.) All you need to know is EVERYTHING HAS BEEN DELICIOUS. 

#2.) Everything seems to be made fresh! From the variety of sausages, ground chuck for hamburgers, etc. Yeah, I'm looking at you all the places I normally go to get my ground meat and there is hidden old meat in the center. Yes, yes I understand that the meat is still fine to use, but why the dishonesty? Just show it as it is! Luckily, this is something I don't have to worry about at The Sausage shop! 

We have also bought some smoked bacon and the quality is unbelievable! 
Have also enjoyed some variety of lunch meat as well as the sliced pastrami-- drool!!! 

They do have a small selection of smoked cheese, but since our family is dairy intolerant we haven't tried it yet. 

They also have a variety of bread rolls to enjoy with your sausages, homemade pickled pickle, sauerkraut, potatoes salad, pasta salad. 

We have tried everything listed above except the cheese. The drinks are also refreshing and easily available for a quick grab and go. 
They also do provide other condiments like the Vienna brand mixed peppers if you want to make a Chicago style dog. 

If cooking isn't your thing, they also seem to provide sandwiches freshly made and ready to go. Saw several people stopping by to just buy a sandwich for lunch and was sooo tempted to try it as well. Will definitely have to in the future.  

*Disclaimer: I'm honestly not a big sausage fan, which was the reason why I was so surprised at how much I really enjoy their sausages. Quality ingredients, freshly made and well done taste made me realize how many people have not actually had a great quality sausage!

We have grilled, baked, sauteed and works great in every way! 

***Bonus note: they also sell these "Meat Sticks" lol that kinda remind me of a more delicious and better slim jim. Works great as a work snack or when hubby wants a little late night snack. Highly recommend! 

Don't forget to tip the staff for their help!

text: I tried this newly opened Pie Five for lunch today.  I'm familiar with the chain, and am usually satisfied with the food and service at my hometown location.  As i ventured in to this new location, i could immediately tell that something was wrong.  The line wasn't moving.  As i got up to the bar, i gave my order to the guy behind the counter.  He was asking me questions in a whisper that i would probably have had to strain to hear if the room had been completely silent.  After nodding yes to a couple things, i just started loudly naming ingredients so he wouldn't misunderstand me.  As he was putting my pizza in the oven, i noticed the line still hadn't moved.  That was when i noticed a small sign (if a post-it note can be a sign) on the register that read "Cash Only".  Seeing it only on one of the two registers, i assumed that it's card reader was broken.  Boy was i wrong.  Their entire credit card system and quite possibly the whole POS system was down.  After yelling at all the customers in line, asking if anybody had cash, i was ushered to the register where I was handed my pizza and drink cup and not told anything about payment.  i went to a table an began to eat.  Assuming that my food was free because of the slow service and broken card system, i was shocked when an employee came around and asked all those that didn't pay to come back up to the register and pay now.  Although i did not believe this was good customer service, i reluctantly went up and paid my bill.  The only silver lining to this entire debacle, was the small amount of humor i found in watching people try to get in the restaurant.  Oh, did i mention they locked the doors without putting a sign up stating a reason.  So people wandered around the building trying all the doors, trying to get in.  In a small way i envy those folks, as they were spared from having their lunch hour ruined.  I guess this place just needs some time to get their act together.  But I'm gonna give it a lot of time.  Like months.

Make reservations cause this place was pretty packed already at 6.

Plenty of cocktails, local beers, wine to choose from.

Came here with a party of 11 and was seated right on time. 

We shared some plates that were so freaking delicious: grits, Mac and cheese, and the fried alligator.  The boudin balls were a bit dry (there's a joke somewhere in that statement) which was a disappointment.

For my main entree I had the Cochon plate.  Although tasty, it wasn't anything uniquely amazing when compared to other nawlins restaurants. 

The atmosphere is trendy and fun but you can honestly get cheaper and tastier food at hole in wall places around town. 

Warning: they do not split checks so imagine having to do math after alcohol....and after the waitress promised she could at the beginning of the meal.

Ok, so it's really hard for me to write about this place because now I want to drive over and indulge.  To sum it up, this place is AMAZING.  I dare say, my favorite restaurant in Philly (and I get around.)

HINT: make a reservation.  This is no "secret" Philly spot.  People are aware of how great it is and you'll want to make sure you can be seated. 

When I called to make the reservation the woman on the phone was incredibly nice.  She asked if we'd like the Chef Table.  This is set up in the back where it's almost like a bar that faces the open kitchen.  I would highly suggest this, a VERY cool experience.  You can see first hand your food being made or zone in and out and see the well oiled machine.  

I can't write a review about this spot without first noting that the service is IMPECCABLE.  Our server suggested wine, and then we decided it would be better for us to get a bottle.  She asked us about price range, (which I thought was very tactful) and then made a suggestion.  I could not get over how quick this service is.  

You NEED to order the grilled octopus, which has forever made any other octopus sub par.  It was absolutely delicious!  I saw a lot of this coming out of the kitchen, so this is clearly a popular dish.  

The Maryland crab toast?  My taste buds literally won't be the same again.  They must put crack on this stuff!

We also had the oysters which were delicious and perfectly shucked.  

I could, and have, rave about this place since going.  It is pricy, but it's worth every penny.  I think if you're celebrating a special occasion, no where else in the city comes close.

Thanks for the feedback, I believe you truly mean what you say about getting the credit card ahead of time for those that are playing golf in the stalls. In terms of people coming in just for food in the bar, I have to say NONE of my friends have EVER had to provide their credit card ahead of time. So I guess your team picks and chooses who they get credit cards from ahead of time. Sounds like you have a lot of work to do to fix it. Please let me know when it is fixed.

Dinner was hit and miss.

The Good:  The tank is beautiful and impressive. We sat toward the front of the restaurant and still had a good view. The calamari appetizer was very good. The crab bisque was delicious. The risotto was excellent. The prices are fair. The valet staff was super friendly and genuinely concerned that we didn't seem to have a good experience. 

The Bad: Although we made a reservation, we still had to wait 22 minutes to be seated (while looking at empty tables), and even then, it wasn't near the tank which is why the gentleman that took our reservation gave us this specific time. 

The iceberg lettuce salad was drenched in olive juice making it completely inedible. Although this is a seafood restaurant, was "out of" 20% of the menu (of course, one of the entrees I wanted.)  The grouper piccata was tasty, but dry. The chicken tortellini tasted like it was boiled in dirty dishwater. 

Although the restaurant only has about 30 tables, there were servers everywhere. Ours, however, showed up every 15 minutes or so. Beverage glasses stayed empty and never checked on the quality of the meal (which we likely would have sent back.) It's billed as a "quiet, under-the-sea" atmosphere, but it seemed remarkably loud. We were seated just outside the entrance to the kitchen and there were no fewer than 3 collisions with wait staff. Fortunately, I made it out of there without food on my back.

I'm really disappointed because this would have been a great place to bring out-of-town guests.

Loved it! A nice addition to the area!

I purchased the Groupon to the Freehouse and was very much looking forward to going. I was not disappointed! The bar was clean and comfortable with a classic English feel. The staff was friendly. We had the crab on toast for an appetizer, amazing. We also had the bangers and mash and the fish pie, both delicious. The bangers and mash were the favorite. The bangers were flavorful and the mash appeared to have grain mustard mixed in. It was served with a yellow mustard and a brown sauce, both bottles looked to be from England. So fun and so nice when a place keeps with the theme. I also had the Elderflower Fizz and it was so yum and classy! My husband had the London Eye, also quite tasty.

We had a wonderful experience at the Freehouse. The reason for 4 and not 5 stars is because I think the menu is a just a little overpriced. But overall I very much enjoyed it and hope to go back soon.

I WISH I could give this place more stars. This is the little grandmom & grandpop place right next to the Tower Theater in Upper Darby- it is SUPER convenient if you're headed in for a show right after. The adorable older couple that owns and runs this place couldn't be any sweeter, are so gracious, and still actively seat and interact with all the guests. The menu is basic- cheesesteaks, burgers, BLTs, french fries. Don't deviate from the basics. I had the turkey burger and it wasn't great. My boyfriend had the chicken cheesesteak and fries and they were both good. The bar's pours are quite strong, which is great. They seat you, get your order, get your drinks, and your food comes right out- even if it's swamped with pre-show folks. The prices could NOT be more reasonable. Even with two top-shelf drinks each, our whole bill was about $40. Their prices probably haven't fluctuated since they opened the place! Unfortunately, they also haven't updated their smoking rules. They let people smoke at the bar, which is definitely illegal and kind of gross for us non smokers. Nonetheless, we always have a great time, helped by the fact that we're always about to see a great show! It's one of those classic, never-been-updated bars. I just wish they could step up the food a little bit and enforce the non-smoking regulations. Still, we'll probably be back before the next Friday night show, it's too convenient not to go.

text:
This is a good location in Beach Dr. with inside and outside seating, but it stops right there.

I went in here with my wife to have a quick snack before our show. It was a bit difficult to choose something we would both like. We settled on the Poutine. All I thought about was the overpowering mustard taste. There really was no other flavor because that took over everything. We ate it up even though we both didn't take care for it bc we knew we wouldn't have much options where we were going.

Our server was done with us as soon as we got our order.  We got our bill, and it took forever to get it back. My wife had to leave to make sure to get our seats ahead of me while I waited.  Never again, no thank you Stillwater!

Spent four days in STL, and managed to fit in two visits to Pastaria! Great food, delicious drinks, fun and relaxed family atmosphere. 

Kale salad was delicious--even without the breadcrumb topping (gluten allergy). Tried the *pappardelle w/ smoked pork, mascarpone & apples. Incredibly rich and delicious, although next time I might actually go for something a little lighter. Although I think this would be PERFECT in late winter. Maybe not as seasonal, but a perfect warm and hearty dish. Husband seemed to really enjoy the pistachio ravioli, and friends/family raved about the bolognese. 

We also tried quite a few of the gelato flavors, all of which I thought were excellent! My favorite this time around involved goat cheese & raspberry (I think. Maybe it was cherry?), but I'm assuming that the flavors rotate on a semi-regular basis. So, I think the best bet is just to go as regularly as humanly possible and test them all out. 

A little pricey for STL, but generally well worth it for the inventive options and quality!



---
*Gluten allergy and had to order the gluten free pasta. My only real complaint (enough so that I can't quite give that 5th star) is the supplement price! I'm just not sure I understand a $6 supplement on an already not particularly cheap pasta dish. I don't think they made the gluten free pasta themselves. And you can get a multi-serving box of the dry gluten free pasta for around $4. So the mark up seems pretty high. And if they are making it in-house, it wasn't any better tasting than the supermarket stuff. So something just seems a little off/frustrating with the pricing.

text:
This place is really a 3.5.  Its good, but it wasn't great.  The look and feel of the restaurant is very clean and precise.  It wasn't very crowded so I cannot comment on the volume as some others have.  It is a bit on the pricey side for sure.  We went with two other couples and there were pluses and minuses across the board.  

The lobster ravioli was pretty spot on.  Decent amount of lobster, flavorful broth.  My husband got the Vegas Strip Steak, which was cooked perfectly but a bit on the small side.  The french fries it came with were completely uneventful...  I had the scallops.  Scallops were huge and it came with a nice rice and peas mixed.  I did enjoy this.

Other folks at the table had the Potato crusted grouper - which was HUGE and she really liked it - the Duck three ways was another huge dish.  No comments if it was great, ok or meh...  but it was finished so I'm guessing it was pretty good!  Another got the special rock shrimp pasta.  Complaint there was it was a bit sandy.

Desserts were all good but hands down the zeppole were the star of the night!

text: Squarely average to below average across the board, except for service which was excellent.  The food was clearly made from quality ingredients, but it was overall bland and underwhelming. Same with the beer, pretty meh.

Just speechless after my appalling experience. Went for sin night and waited half the time just for drinks. The male bartender was clearly over his head, drunk, an idiot, or all of the above. There was another lady bartender who was going as fast as she could, but there were just too many people. 

I wasn't ordering something with a ton of ingredients. I ordered beers. and shots. This was met with a confused look, and he'd run around looking for the bottle of Jameson *it was on the left by the terminal*, and then come back and ask me what I wanted again. They lost my tab and had to re-ask me what I'd ordered prior. This, bar managers, is an easy way to lose a lot of money. I was 4 drinks in, how was I supposed to know what my boyfriend may have put on my tab? 

The worst part of my experience was the manager (or clipboard holding, beer counting dude not in a uniform) was either clueless or unconcerned with the large amount of frustrated patrons. He was behind the bar for a second. He didn't direct the idle barback to help, or jump in and get to pouring. He just let 50+ service industry folks get pissed and leave. 

Bowling was ok. Was told I didn't need shoes, and the alley's pins were on strings, which kind of inhibited their natural patterns of falling. I feel like one could master a different type of bowling from playing here.

Great restaurant on a boat overlooking the Delaware river and Ben Franklin bridge and also the Philadelphia 76ers practice facility. We went during their happy hour to grab some drinks while the weather was still beautiful and I say this cause we were expecting heavy down pour later in the evening. They have multiple levels in the restaurant including the open bar on the top most level. However, the open bar is only for drinks and they don't serve any food there. But you can order food from the lower level and bring it with you to the open bar. 

So we grabbed a couple of seats overlooking the river. Nicely dressed coincidentally for a nice boat party. Bar tender Chris was amazing. I love dark and stormy so he made me one. Although he did not have the usual dark rum he used another rum which did not look as dark as I expected it to be but nevertheless it tasted really good.

Their food menu looked good too. But since we had dinner plans elsewhere we did not grab any food from here. The interiors of this restaurant looks very classy and elegant. You would definitely love this place for a fancy dinner or open bar for a casual time with your friends and family. 

I definitely recommend this place to everyone who is visiting Philly and wants to explore the water front. Remember not many restaurants in this part of the city anyways. So why not grab a drink here at this beautiful location.

I am super hype that Seorabol CC is finally up and running! I've been eagerly waiting for this spot to open since the Olney location is great, but I can't say it's worth the hike from my neighborhood in the suburbs. Sorry to the kbbq fans who love cooking their own meat, but you'll have to go to Olney since there aren't table grills here. 

My friends and I stopped in as the first official customers for the soft opening and encountered very, very friendly staff. The soft opening menu is pared down (especially if you're used to the pages long barbecue spread), but it has all the essentials plus a few extra fancy Seorabol picks.

I'm a kimchi jjigae fiend through and through, so I sat down with that while my friends got the jaeyook bokkeum, which is basically marinated pork and vegetables stir-fried and served with rice, which I also love. The flavors were all there, and I honestly just can't wait to see what the full-fledged menu turns out to be. Ddeokguk? Ddukbaegi bulgogi? I'm ready!

J. Alexander's is a chain of premium American restaurants. They offer a large menu, featuring sandwiches, steak and even sushi. We stopped by for lunch and started with the calamari. The seafood was fresh and the breading was crisp and tasty. 

For my main course, I went for the crab cakes; I requested they leave the sauce on the side (it came with Dijon and spicy mayo). The crab cakes come with fries and coleslaw, but I substituted the healthier orzo salad and broccoli. The broccoli was flavorful and fresh, as was the cold orzo salad. The crab cakes were fresh and teeming with large chunks of meat. The spicy mayo didn't do much for me and I'm glad I got it on the side. 

My tablemate ordered a medium well filet. The steak was a solid medium rare - still plenty of blood and purple. He pointed it out to the waitress and was met with a shrug, not the best customer service (this is why I've only given 3 stars, no excuse for that when you're paying top dollar). 

We finished the meal with some key lime pie and it was pretty good.

Stopped into Toups for appetizers and it was a great choice. I had the boudin which was good, the crackling was some of the best I ever had. The highlight though was the great meat plate that featured a lot of great housemade meat items. The best of all was the hogshead cheese. I haven't had the dinner so I cannot give the full five stars but I'm willing to get they are great also.

Besides the nice, clean sitting area, tentative services, reasonable pricing, easy parking that all the criteria a good restaurant required, this place offered some unique dishes that stand out from all the Mediterrian restaurants at Bay area. We tried the followings:
Baked Hummus- The huge fresh bake bread as big as a basket ball was super impressive and tasty. The hummus was baked in a shallow clay plate so the edge was crunchy with melt cheese , the added on sausages on top. Tasted so good, of course , with the fresh bread. 
Grill Lamb chop-  Four pieces of grilled lamb chops with rice, salad, red cabbage. Good flavor, good texture of the meat, I liked it. 
Grill Mediterrean sea bass - The fish was perfect- fresh, right amount of seasoning, good grilling technique, no medium or small fish bones. The fish meat was easy to pick, fine texture and flavor, free from the fishy smell.   It was the best grill whole fish I ever had in town! 
Kunefe-This was a fine shedded cheese dessert baked to golden brown and soaked in sweet syrup.  The cheese was crunchy ouside, elastic inside with the chopped pistachio garnish. I am normally not a cheese eater, yet this dish made me fall in love with it. Such a yummy dessert!
It was a very satisfied meal . I was happy  we had the  Turkish  dinner here.

Stop reading this Yelp post right now and go pack yourself a bowl at Buddha Bowls. This place is FIRE! Get the pizza bowl or the BBQ bowl in the sourdough bread bowl and get the combo with either buddha bread sticks or the "volcano" which is a delicious mess of sour dough bread covered in freshly cut strawberries, whip cream and chocolate. Their bread sticks are super delicious in combination with their marinara sauce they give with it. Overall super delicious and super filling! I usually share a bowl 'cuz bowls are better that way:) and because the bread bowls are huge lol

I hate... absolutely HATE giving one star reviews... but we go to get a sandwich at 8:10pm on a Wednesday night (tonight) and they are closed??? The sign says 9pm. Ugh! 

I've been to this location previously... its ever been anything to write home about. It's annoying they don't accept coupons... the people who work there are ok, sometimes I go in and they are spending more time talking to their friends than paying attention to my order... but it's a sandwich... I don't need that much attention... but geeze... closed an hour before you're supposed to be, no signage, just closed. 

I'm grumpy because I AM STARVING! 

There is another location off Sparks blvd that I will now go to, I give up on this location.

Oh, and their phone number is disconnected... So, there's that.

I asked for my large drink and chilli packets with dilling sauces for my nuggets.  She hands over the coke and looks at me like i am crazy. Boring, over-priced burgers... more than $25 for just two burgers. No drinks, no fries. Wouldn't honor axxess deal. Won't be back.

I've enjoyed dining-in here, as well as picking up many orders to-go. Taziki's serves huge portions of fresh, flavorful food very quickly! Prices are higher than other nearby fast food options, but this isnt typical fast food; the quality is worth it.

The lamb gyro is incredible! So tender, and big! I also LOVE their tomato & cucumber salad. That's my usual order. Sometimes I mix it up with roasted potatoes as my side, but since the gyro comes with potato chips anyway, I try to add the healthier side. As my office is currently in the same plaza, Taziki's is our go-to restaurant for working lunches. And because I'm usually the one who picks up the order, I've seen the salads with salmon & chicken, both grilled & blackened... they look so fresh & delicious, especially the Mediterranean. And their baklava is fantastic, although I don't get that every time. We do often get the hummus &/or Taziki dip with baked pita chips as an appetizer - I could make a light meal of that. 

Taziki's also serves wine but unfortunately I haven't had the opportunity to try any of it, since I'm there during lunch time, and eating with my boss. Also, on Wednesdays only, they have a spanakopita roll-up with chicken that I want to try. 

The service here is always fantastic... Attentive, prompt, and friendly. I hope I to eat here a few more times before my my office moves. But I'll be back anyway. I love that lamb gyro!

My husband and I went here for the first time tonight after a particularly stressful few days. The waitress was a delight-very attentive and friendly. I ordered sushi deluxe. Everything was so fresh. Some of the freshest sushi I have ever had (and I have had a lot of sushi in lots of major cities). When it arrived, it was so beautiful I just wanted to look at it. It was too beautiful to eat!! I had to take a picture!  The only thing better than the way it looked was the taste. Very yummy. My husband got volcano roll and the presentation was lovely and he said it tasted awesome. The chef surprised us with a warm fried banana with whipped cream, drizzled with chocolate. Yum!!  I can't wait to go back! And to tell all my friends. Like them on Facebook.
